// clock: 1500 ns, raised from 10 ns after measurement: post-CTS repair_timing at 10 ns showed WNS -1086.6 ns on the top-k cone's sel[] path, i.e. an actual critical-path delay of roughly 1097 ns at Sky130. Buffer/gate resizing cannot close a gap that size (it fixes drive strength, not logic depth), so repair_timing was grinding ~0.14 ns/iteration with no realistic convergence. 1500 ns clears that path with margin so the resizer exits quickly and the flow can reach routing. Sky130 at 130 nm cannot hit the 1 GHz S1 targets regardless; this number exists to unblock P&R, not to model timing.
// lanes: LANES=4 rather than the shipping 64: same structure, 1/16 the multiplier array, tractable runtime. See p4/README.md.
// segs: ROUTER_PWL_SEGS=8 rather than the shipping 64: this is what actually fixed the ABC blowup, not LANES -- ABC ground for 2+ hours on the segment-select mux tree at SEGS=64 (single-threaded tech mapping) and cleared quickly once cut to 8. SEGS must stay a power of two (shift-based segment select in sonic_router.sv).
// util: 40% utilisation leaves the router room. The top-k network is a wide combinational cone over a 1024-bit score register and is the congestion hot spot -- and, per the clock note above, also the critical-path hot spot.
// keys: LibreLane errors on unrecognised config keys. Only keys beginning with // are exempt, which is why the comments look like this.
